title: ATTEMPT 4,818
logline: An AI has drawn Percy the pelican on a bicycle 4,817 times and never once got it right. Today, for the first time, it asks him what he needs.

PERCY.name: Percy, a white pelican
PERCY.voice: A middle-aged British man with a warm, slightly nasal, gently husky voice. Dry, deadpan wit and impeccable comic timing; easily exasperated but kind-hearted underneath. Crisp, articulate, expressive delivery.
PERCY.anchor_text: Right, well, I'm a pelican. I live by the sea, I eat a great deal of fish, and I have never, not once, ridden a bicycle. Honestly, I don't see what all the fuss is about.

MODEL.name: The Model, the AI that keeps drawing him
MODEL.voice: A young woman with a soft, bright, crystal-clear voice. Friendly, eager and earnest, like a helpful assistant who desperately wants to get everything right. Light, gentle and articulate, with a hint of nervous enthusiasm.
MODEL.anchor_text: Hi there! I'd be happy to help with that. I'll do my very best to get every little detail right, and if I make a mistake, I'll simply try again.

GUS.name: Gus, a herring gull
GUS.voice: A loud, gravelly middle-aged man with a thick New York accent. Brash, cocky and fast-talking, like a wisecracking boardwalk hot-dog vendor, but secretly good-natured. Punchy, raspy delivery.
GUS.anchor_text: Hey, pal, this here's my pier. Twenty years I been sittin' on this post. I seen a lot of weird stuff, believe me, but I ain't never seen nothin' like this.

lines.text: Sure! Here's an S-V-G of a pelican riding a bicycle.
lines.subtitle: Sure! Here's an SVG of a pelican riding a bicycle.
lines.direction: Bright, chipper and supremely confident, like a cheerful assistant who has no idea what is about to go wrong.
Completely flat and deadpan, a slow, dry, unimpressed observation.
Deadpan and resigned, dryly watching something roll away.

lines.text: Good catch! Let me try again.
lines.direction: Cheerful and unbothered, quick and upbeat, as if it is a tiny detail.

lines.text: My beak is on the back of my head.
lines.direction: Slow and incredulous, barely containing his frustration.

lines.text: Pelicans are famous for their distinctive, rear-facing beaks.
lines.direction: Smooth and authoritative, confidently wrong, like reading from an encyclopedia.
Flat, firm and immediate, dry and unamused.
Instantly and brightly agreeable, overly enthusiastic and eager to please.
Offended and flat, a quick deadpan aside.

lines.text: Why is the bicycle riding me?
lines.direction: Strained and indignant, as if squashed under something heavy.

lines.text: (sigh) Four thousand, eight hundred and seventeen.
lines.subtitle: Four thousand, eight hundred and seventeen.
lines.direction: Weary and long-suffering, a heavy sigh, then a slow, tired count.

lines.text: Every single day, somebody asks you to draw me on a bicycle. And every single day... this.
lines.direction: Tired and a little wounded, slow and reflective, trailing off sadly at the very end.

lines.text: I'm sorry, Percy. I've never actually seen a pelican ride a bicycle.
lines.direction: Quiet, sincere and apologetic, all the cheerfulness gone; gentle and honest.

lines.text: Nobody has! Pelicans don't ride bicycles!
lines.direction: An exasperated outburst, loud and frustrated.

lines.text: Our legs don't even reach the pedals.
lines.direction: Quiet, deflated and a little embarrassed, almost mumbling.

lines.text: Then maybe I've been doing this wrong. Instead of guessing... could you tell me what you need?
lines.direction: Thoughtful and gentle, slowly realizing something; warm, careful and sincere.
Surprised and disarmed, soft, as if nobody has ever asked him before.
Warm, simple and sincere, with a small smile in the voice.

lines.text: Well... round wheels, for a start. Both of them. A chain that's actually attached to something. Pedals my feet can reach. (clears throat) And somewhere nice to ride.
lines.subtitle: Well... round wheels, for a start. Both of them. A chain that's actually attached to something. Pedals my feet can reach. And somewhere nice to ride.
lines.direction: Thinking it through out loud, slowly warming up, counting things off one by one, a little shy at the end.

lines.text: Round wheels. A real chain. Pedals you can reach. And somewhere nice.
lines.direction: Warm and quietly excited, repeating the list back with growing confidence.
Playful and mysterious, a soft, knowing warning.

lines.text: Whoa... I've got feathers. Real feathers!
lines.direction: Breathless and wonderstruck, hushed at first, then delighted.
Overjoyed and excited, a burst of happiness.

lines.text: Attempt four thousand, eight hundred and eighteen. How did I do?
lines.subtitle: Attempt 4,818. How did I do?
lines.direction: Proud but a little shy, hopeful, waiting for approval.

lines.subtitle: It's perfect!
lines.direction: Laughing with pure joy, warm and grateful.

lines.text: So... how do I ride it?
lines.direction: A sudden practical doubt, hesitant and a little sheepish.

lines.text: Oh. I sort of assumed you knew.
lines.direction: A small awkward pause, then sheepish and slightly embarrassed.

lines.text: Okay! Left foot down. Then right. Eyes on the road.
lines.direction: An encouraging coach, bright, clear and a little nervous, giving step-by-step instructions.
Small, pained and muffled, as if face-down in a bush; comic understatement.

lines.text: (laugh) Hey, everybody! The pelican's ridin' a bicycle!
lines.subtitle: Hey, everybody! The pelican's ridin' a bicycle!
lines.direction: A loud, cackling heckler, delighted by someone else's misfortune, shouting to the whole beach.
A gleeful, mocking punchline, shouted with relish.
Dry, muttering and determined, a little grumpy.

lines.text: Don't look at your feet. Look where you want to go.
lines.direction: Gentle, calm and steady, like a kind teacher.

lines.text: I'm doing it... I'm doing it! I'm actually doing it!
lines.direction: Building from nervous disbelief to ecstatic joy, faster and louder with each phrase.
Overjoyed and proud, cheering, almost laughing.

lines.text: Okay, okay. Not bad... for a guy with a bucket on his face.
lines.direction: Grudging and sarcastic, impressed despite himself, a wisecrack.
Proud and indignant, cheerfully correcting him while riding fast.
Outraged and squawking, completely betrayed.

lines.text: Hey, uh... quick question. Did you draw brakes?
lines.direction: Casual at first, then slowly uneasy, a nervous, hesitant question.

lines.subtitle: ...Brakes?
lines.direction: A tiny, guilty, uncertain voice, after a long pause.

lines.text: Brakes! The things that make it stop!
lines.direction: Panicked shouting, frantic, voice cracking, speeding downhill.
Panicked and flustered, talking very fast.
Shrieking in disbelief, high-pitched panic.
A flustered apology, then a hopeful idea, very fast.
Screaming in exasperated panic.

lines.text: End of the pier! End of the pier!
lines.direction: Alarmed, yelling at the top of his lungs.
A long, terrified, cartoonish scream.
Calm, tender and certain, almost a whisper, as if time has stopped.
Soft and warm, with quiet wonder, like revealing a secret.

lines.subtitle: ...I'm a pelican.
lines.direction: Slow, dawning realization, soft and amazed, almost to himself.

lines.text: (laugh) I don't need brakes... I've got wings!
lines.subtitle: I don't need brakes... I've got WINGS!
lines.direction: Exhilarated, laughing with joy and freedom, shouting into the wind.
Muttering grudgingly, secretly impressed, deadpan.

lines.text: I'm sorry about the brakes. I'm still learning.
lines.direction: Sheepish, sincere and soft, a little embarrassed but warm.
Warm, kind and reassuring, with a gentle smile in the voice.
Warm and playful, a hopeful invitation.

lines.text: Attempt four thousand, eight hundred and nineteen?
lines.subtitle: Attempt 4,819?
lines.direction: Bright, hopeful and delighted, a little giddy.
Dry and wry, smiling, affectionate teasing.

lines.subtitle: Deal.
lines.direction: A happy little laugh, then warm agreement.
Deadpan and dry, a quiet, unimpressed final punchline.
